title: Integrate Pico–Franka into Robot Capture
goal: Adapt the existing Pico-controlled single-arm Franka workflow to the company's Robot Capture (Shucai) workbench while preserving its existing workbench and upload capabilities.
doneWhen: The selected integration boundary and data-recording owner are explicitly approved.
The Franka control path is integrated without bypassing Franka Desk protections or allowing the web process to directly own real-time robot control.
The company workbench behavior outside the Franka embodiment remains unchanged.
The resulting collection and upload artifact format, provenance, and acceptance checks are defined and verified at the applicable level.
decisions: Development worktree is /home/modelbest/Project/RLinf-Franka/robot_capture_franka-franka-feature on branch feature/franka-robot-capture.

Initial discovery is read-only. Robot Capture is the company NiceGUI workbench with camera, HDF5 conversion, and upload queues; PiperTeleRecord_web is a separately adapted snapshot that added teleoperation supervision and UI while retaining the Robot Capture application.
The Release Franka product currently owns live Pico-to-Franka control and legacy pickle-to-LeRobot collection through scripts/run_pico_session.sh; it is not itself a Robot Capture web application.

Approved: follow the Piper model. Robot Capture owns the production recording artifact, HDF5 conversion, upload, and unchanged workbench; the Franka/Pico path supplies the control and synchronized robot telemetry.

Approved delivery boundary: create the independent robot_capture_franka repository from the company robot-capture source baseline; preserve robot-capture unchanged. The integration feature branch is feature/franka-robot-capture.
The user authorized publishing the initial repository baseline to https://github.com/TBLboy/robot_capture_franka.git using Git identity TBLboy <1218740205@qq.com>.

Approved camera requirement: support the current two-camera Franka deployment and future three-camera dual-arm deployment without requiring a separate product; retain explicit camera roles and an HDF5 representation that permits the optional third view.

Approved control boundary: the workbench supervises a separate Franka control process which exclusively owns live robot control. The workbench only requests lifecycle actions and reads state plus actual issued control targets; its record control starts/stops data capture only.

Approved recording gate: robot-data recording requires all configured cameras online, a healthy Franka control process, and fresh robot state plus actual issued-control samples; otherwise it must not start a robot-data recording.

Approved data scope: per synchronized record retain Franka joint state, end-effector pose, gripper state, actual Pico-derived Cartesian control target/action, host timestamps, and camera frames/timestamps. Assess Robot Capture's pipeline against the Franka control loop and require camera capture of at least 30 Hz.
Approved UI workflow: add a separate Franka teleoperation workbench page, following the Piper separation between control lifecycle/safety operations and the existing capture page.
The approved requirement baseline is recorded in robot_capture_franka/docs/franka-integration-requirements.md.

Design discovery: the unmodified Robot Capture implementation is structurally fixed to three left/center/right cameras across its camera manager, synchronizer, recorder, UI, device discovery, and HDF5 exporter. It supports only Orbbec and RealSense SDK backends, not the Release ZED UVC backend.

Design discovery: Release scripts/run_pico_session.sh starts an RLinf/Ray collection worker that opens the same cameras and owns legacy pickle collection. It cannot run concurrently with Robot Capture as the production recorder because camera ownership conflicts and it does not expose an IPC telemetry/control-target contract.

Approved: do not reuse the Release Ray/RLinf collection worker as the live service. Extract the necessary validated Pico/Franka control behavior into a dedicated control worker that owns no camera and publishes passive state, actual issued Cartesian targets, and health through local IPC.

Implementation design is documented in robot_capture_franka/docs/franka-integration-design.md: configured camera roles with ZED UVC, Unix-socket worker control/telemetry, strict fresh-data recording gates, and versioned Franka HDF5 data.

Implementation began with a dependency-free versioned passive telemetry contract and bounded timestamp history in robot_capture_franka/franka/telemetry.py. It validates 7-DOF robot state and guarded issued Cartesian targets, rejects replayed samples, and has no live-hardware imports.

Added a workbench-owned UVC camera backend for ZED colour-video nodes. It accepts explicit uvc/zed_uvc/v4l2 configuration, lazily imports OpenCV, requires the configured stable video path to exist, and preserves existing RealSense/Orbbec backend selection. Dynamic two/three-role pipeline refactoring remains next.

Implemented a local Unix-socket lifecycle client, process supervisor, and fail-closed worker protocol. Its only accepted commands are lifecycle/safety operations; no API accepts a Cartesian target. The worker defaults to an unavailable backend until a Release-compatible Franky/Pico backend is ported, so no unfinished path can claim live robot control.
Integrated a strict Franka recording readiness hook: when enabled, recording requires fresh worker state and issued-action telemetry rather than falling back to video-only data.

Generalized the core synchronizer, recorder, session metadata, preview API, and HDF5 camera export around configured camera roles and a configured reference camera. The record-page preview now uses configured roles; legacy device-discovery behavior remains a follow-up adaptation.

The standalone worker includes an opt-in Release-compatible PicoExpert/Franky/Robotiq backend. It keeps camera ownership out of the worker, uses explicit TCP pose bounds plus Franky's existing adjacent-target guard, composes controller deltas from the grip-edge pose instead of accumulating them, and leaves reset disabled until operator validation. franka_worker.enabled remains false by default.

User approved migration of the shared Release hardware configuration. Active robot_capture_franka/config.yaml now selects UVC global+wrist ZED nodes at 30 Hz, and ignored franka-worker.json contains the existing robot IP, Pico IPC endpoint, Robotiq stable serial path, and compliance values; franka_worker.enabled remains false.

Operator confirmed on 2026-10-20 that the staged workbench startup reaches ready and controls the Franka arm on the two-camera rig. Reset remains disabled and robot-data recording is still unvalidated.

2026-10-21: operator approved fixing recorded-data correctness (float64 robot timestamps, (N,) scalar columns, schema_version 2) even though it touches HDF5 export, and merging the feature branch into main.
Merge method: local --no-ff merge of feature/franka-robot-capture into main, creating 2786157; the merged tree passes 73 offline tests. Nothing pushed to origin.
